Presence:-
Mr. Harshpal Sekhon, learned counsel for the petitioners.
Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, learned Addl. C.S.C. with Mr. S.S.
Chaudhary, learned S.C. and Mr. Hargovind Pant, learned B.H. for
the State.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
These writ petitions have been filed by the
petitioner(s) seeking parity of pay scale with Data Entry
Operator working with the respondent employed through
U.P.N.L.
2. Since common questions of fact and law are
involved in these petitions, therefore, these petitions are
clubbed together and decided by this common judgment.
However, for the sake of brevity and convenience, facts of
WPSS No.1808 of 2026 alone are being considered and
discussed.
3. Petitioner was engaged as a contractual Data
Entry Operator under the Samagra Shiksha Uttarakhand
1

UKHC010120872026
2026:UHC:5786
at Block Resource Centre (B.R.C.) Tarikhet, District-Almora, in the year 2008, initially for a period of one year
and subsequently the period of his engagement was
extended and he is working on the said post till date as
contractual Data Entry Operator.
4. Petitioner is being paid ₹5,500/- per month as
consolidate remuneration which was enhanced from time to
time and at present he is getting ₹18,000/- as
remuneration. The petitioner claimed parity with Data
Entry Operator who were engaged with the respondent-Department through U.P.N.L. and are getting a monthly
remuneration of ₹27,299.63/-.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that
since the petitioner is discharging the same function as are
being discharged by the Data Entry Operator employed
through U.P.N.L. therefore he is entitled to get the same
remuneration on the basis of "equal pay for equal work".
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner further
submits that for the said relief the petitioner has filed a
representation to respondent no.2-State Project Director for
redressal of his grievance and he submits that if a direction
is issued to respondent no.2-State Project Director to
decide the said representation, within a stipulated time, the
ends of justice would be met.
7. Learned counsel for the State submits that the
representation which the petitioner indicated is not by
petitioner rather it is through his Union and therefore it
would be difficult for respondent no.2 to decide the same,
however he submits that if the petitioner may be permitted
to file a fresh representation to respondent no.2 within a
stipulated time, the respondent no.2 shall decide the same
if directed by the Court.
8. In such view of the matter, all the writ petitions
2

UKHC010120872026
2026:UHC:5786
are finally stand disposed of. Petitioner of each of these writ
petitions are permitted to file a representation ventilating
their grievance regarding equal pay for equal work at par
with the Data Entry Operator engaged through U.P.N.L.
within ten days' from today and if such a representation is
submitted by the petitioner(s) individually, the respondent
no.2 shall decide the same within a period of eight weeks'
from the date of receipt of the representations, strictly in
accordance with law.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
